articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Cowboys get a break by facing shorthanded Buccaneers
articles.summary: The Buccaneers will start an undrafted rookie QB for the second straight game.
articles.body:
Sometimes the NFL makes bad decisions on its primetime games. But there are other instances in which the league is just unlucky.

When the schedule came out in May, the Thursday night game for Week 5 was a reasonable choice. The Dallas Cowboys are always interesting and were an offseason darling. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers struggled in the second half of last season but they had plenty of stars and were the preseason favorite to win the NFC South. At the very least, Buccaneers at Cowboys should have held our interest.

Nobody figured on the Bucs being this bad by Week 5.

The Buccaneers were 0-3 when they lost Baker Mayfield to a dislocated right thumb. They had a curious backup quarterback plan for the season, going with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. When Mayfield went down, Daniels became the first undrafted rookie quarterback since the AFL/NFL merger in 1970 to start a game in Week 4 or earlier. And the results were predictable, with Daniels playing well considering the circumstances but Tampa Bay still losing 17-14 to the Green Bay Packers to fall to 0-4. The Buccaneers are 2-11 in their last 13 games. Head coach Todd Bowles might be on the hot seat.

And while anything can happen in the NFL, facing a winless Buccaneers team with an undrafted rookie at quarterback is clearly a fortunate break for the Cowboys. Dallas rallied last week to beat the Houston Texans 34-30. That bumped Dallas' record back to 2-2, which is not bad shape considering the rest of the NFC East has issues. The Cowboys have their own issues too. The Cowboys defense is 31st in EPA ( expected points added ) allowed per play, ahead of only the Detroit Lions. The offense has been good, as expected. The defense hasn't shown much improvement from last season, when it gave up the most points in franchise history.

The good news for the Cowboys is the Buccaneers, in their current status, are one of the few teams that might not be able to exploit that defense.

It depends if you think the Buccaneers' season is over at 0-4. It might be. Perhaps Baker Mayfield can return as early as Week 6, and if so, 1-4 in the NFC South isn't completely out of the race. No team in NFL history has made the playoffs after starting 0-5 though. Considering the Buccaneers have shown so few signs of life, the game probably means more to the Cowboys. They're 2-2 and trailing only the New York Giants, who are without quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the season, in the NFC East. A loss to Jalon Daniels and the Buccaneers wouldn't just be bad in the NFC East, it would cause a firestorm that would last for 10 days until Dallas plays again.

Lamb has been an elite receiver for many years, and he's on pace to smash his career highs. Lamb is averaging an NFL-best 124.5 yards per game, which is well ahead of his former career best of 102.9 yards. He also is averaging 9.3 receptions per game, and he has never been above eight per game. Last week's monster game, with 17 catches for 189 yards and a game-winning touchdown, was an extension of his hot streak. It was Lamb's third straight 100-yard game. The Buccaneers' pass defense has been solid. It hasn't allowed more than 245 passing yards in a game this season. But it will be a challenge to slow down Lamb, the hottest receiver in the NFL.

This game was Cowboys -3.5 and it was -9.5 on the lookahead, due to how bad Tampa Bay has looked (and Baker Mayfield's injury), along with the potency of Dallas' offense. The Bucs are 0-4 both straight up and against the spread, and the Jalon Daniels-led offense only put up 134 passing yards and 14 points against Green Bay. While Daniels should be able to throw on the Cowboys D, it's hard to see Tampa Bay matching points here. A raucous Cowboys Stadium in primetime is also very different than a 1 p.m. ET start at home on a Sunday. This line has come down a bit, but ranges from Cowboys -7.5 to -8.5 in the market. I expect Dallas to cover — as do public bettors loading up on them.

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

The Cowboys are expected to roll over Tampa Bay in the Week 5 opener, but you know what they say in this league, Any Given Thursday. Here are three fantasy themes to track as you watch the game.

1. Will Jalon Daniels be improved in his second start? Daniels was put in a difficult position last week, an undrafted rookie asked to start a month into his NFL career. Predictably, he produced just 148 passing yards and no one in the Buccaneers' offense got past 40 yards receiving. We're pulling for Daniels, in part so we can squeeze some value from the Tampa Bay receiving room.

2. What's the distribution in the Dallas passing game? CeeDee Lamb went bonkers in the win at Houston last week, a 17-189-1 detonation on 21 targets. Meanwhile, George Pickens was limited to just three targets, though he did produce 75 yards and drew two defensive penalties. Lamb has clearly reestablished himself as the alpha in Dallas, but the Cowboys know it's important to keep Pickens engaged, too.

3. What will Bucky Irving's usage look like? Although Irving had a credible 16-61-0 rushing line last week, teammates stole from his bottom line — Sean Tucker punched in a short touchdown run, and Kenneth Gainwell had a touchdown catch. Perhaps more concerning for Irving managers, he wasn't targeted in the passing game. Irving had seven catches in the season opener at Cincinnati — that feels like a year ago.

Check out more of Scott's work at the Yahoo Sports fantasy hub .

articles.title: NFL referees’ jobs outside the league: From roughly $50,000 firefighter roles to $240,000 aerospace software careers
articles.summary: The NFL season lasts for roughly five to six months.
articles.body: The NFL season lasts for roughly five to six months. During the other six months, most players spend time with their families, prepare for the upcoming season, or attend to their commercial commitments.But what happens to the referees? Nobody seems to know - or even wonder! That is, unless fans are accusing them of being biased against their team or favoring Patrick Mahomes too much.Scrutiny also cyberspace spikes when, out of the blue, a referee's behavior toward a player crosses the line. For instance, two referees were recently suspended for unprofessional conduct during Week 4 games.While suspensions like this are intriguingly rare, they raise a valid question: what do referees do during the offseason when the NFL isn’t taking up their time? As it turns out, most of them have full-time jobs.NFL referees have full time careers outside of footballNFL referees have full-time careers outside of football while officiating in the league, a fact recently reported by Bleacher Report on Instagram.Bill Vinovich is a certified public accountant, Carl Cheffers is a sales manager at a car battery company, Ron Torbet is an attorney, Adrian Hill is an aerospace software engineer, and Clay Martin is a retired high school administrator and basketball coach.Likewise, Shawn Hochuli is a financial advisor, Alex Kemp is an insurance agent, Scott Campbell is a firefighter, and Tony Josselyn is a probation officer.NFL officials bring diverse professional backgroundsPer the 2026 NFL roster, 121 officials are assigned to 17 crews, plus two swing officials for an umpire and a back judge. These two swing officials move between the crews through the season. Seven new officials replaced seven officials who retired or were otherwise not retained at the end of the 2025 season.Six new replay assistants were added for the 2026 season to replace three who were promoted to replay official and three who were not retained.The Football Zebras website particularly highlights the outside occupations of many officials, clearly underscoring how diverse their professional backgrounds and current professions are.Land Clark is a chief building official, while Alan Eck is a tax manager. Tim Podraza is a business performance consultant, while John Hussey is a nonprofit founder and CEO.Mike Carr is an athletic director, while Julie Johnson is a coordinator of intramural sports. Greg Wilson is a retired police officer, while Artenzia Young-Seigler is a college professor.Mearl Robinson is a retired U.S. Air Force instructor, while Desiree Abrams is a food safety enforcement coordinator.How much does an NFL referee make in a yearLast Word On Sports’ Founder and CEO Michael Kovacs reported in June 2026 that an entry-level NFL referee with one to three years of experience makes $100,000 to $150,000 annually. A mid-career NFL referee with three to five years of experience takes home $150,000 to $200,000.An experienced NFL referee with five to eight years of experience has an estimated annual salary of $200,000 to $250,000. A crew chief or top official has an estimated annual salary above $250,000.This gives us an idea of an NFL referee's gridiron salary. However, if we look at their full-time careers outside of football, their average earnings - regardless of experience - might be much higher than expected.For instance, Scott Campbell, Nate Jones, and Dave Hawkshaw all work as firefighters. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the 2025 median pay for firefighters was $59,280 per year and $28.50 per hour.For instance, take Scott Campbell: with four years of NFL experience, his annual referee salary is estimated to be between $150,000 and $200,000. When you add his firefighter earnings, his total annual income ranges from $209,000 to $259,000.As for Adrian Hill, who has 17 years of NFL experience, his estimated referee salary is over $250,000. He also works as an aerospace software engineer. According to ZipRecruiter data from October 2026, the estimated salary for that role is $147,000 per year and $70 per hour. Combining both incomes brings his yearly total to around $397,000.This dual-income reality applies to almost every NFL referee. They maintain full-time careers outside of football because the sport isn’t a year-round business - it is a six-month circus! For the remaining six months of the year, a man must earn! To keep himself busy and his family well-fed.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: La NFL se viste de hispana
articles.standfirst: Durante tres días, NFL Culture Club Madrid ofrecerá conciertos y sesiones musicales, exposiciones, proyecciones, encuentros, entrevistas, experiencias gastronómicas
articles.summary: NFL España presenta NFL Culture Club Madrid, proyecto que contará con conciertos, sesiones musicales, exposiciones y muchas cosas más durante los próximos tres días
articles.body: En la Fundación Ortega-Marañón, en pleno corazón de Madrid, NFL España ha presentado NFL Culture Club Madrid, una experiencia multidisciplinar que busca entrelazar la cultura latina, española y estadounidense a través de la moda, la música, el arte, con el fútbol americano como punto de encuentro. El acto de inauguración ha contado con la presencia de Rafael De los Santos, presidente de la NFL en España, quien ha querido dar la bienvenida a todo el mundo a este nuevo proyecto: "Es un placer abrir esta primera edición junto a la Comunidad de Madrid. La NFL se vive de muchas maneras, dentro y fuera del terreno de juego. Es de esta idea de dónde sale todo. Durante estos tres días la música, la gastronomía, el cine y la moda nos van a permitir unir España Latinoamérica y Estados Unidos a través de los artistas y sus ideas. Ojalá salgáis de aquí con una nueva canción o una nueva historia que contar pero sobre todo con muchas ganas de NFL". Durante tres días, NFL Culture Club Madrid ofrecerá conciertos y sesiones musicales, exposiciones, proyecciones, encuentros, entrevistas, experiencias gastronómicas y contenidos vinculados a algunos de los principales referentes de la cultura y la creatividad de España, Latinoamérica y Estados Unidos. La iniciativa nace en un momento en el que la cultura hispana ejerce una influencia internacional cada vez mayor y conecta a millones de personas a ambos lados del Atlántico a través del idioma, la música, la gastronomía, la moda y el arte. NFL Culture Club Madrid utilizará el deporte como un nuevo punto de encuentro entre estas comunidades. La música será uno de los grandes ejes, con actuaciones de Vreno Yg y Raul Clyde, y sesiones de La Granja Sound, mami y Miss Aleta, además de encuentros con los artistas, contenido exclusivo, experiencias para los fans o la sala RIMAS Room, una de las compañías discográficas más influyentes de la música latina y casa de artistas como Bad Bunny. Habrá gastronomía con el Tailgate Tapas reinterpretando el tradicional previo a los partidos de la NFL; una exposición fotográfica reinterpretando algunos de los grandes símbolos del fútbol americano a partir de referencias de la tradición y la cultura hispana; una selección de cortometrajes, documentales y producciones que exploran las conexiones entre España, Latinoamérica y Estados Unidos a través del deporte, la creatividad, la identidad y la comunidad; la iniciativa de moda FRSH, con una colección y propuestas de customización vinculadas al universo de NFL Culture Club Madrid; y un programa de charlas abiertas al público que conectará las distintas disciplinas. Jueves 8 de octubre · 18:00–21:30h · Vreno Yg · La Granja Sound · Exposición de fotografía · FRSH · RIMAS Room · Cine y gastronomía Viernes 9 de octubre · 18:00–21:30h · Toro · mami · Exposición de fotografía · FRSH · RIMAS Room · Cine y gastronomía Sábado 10 de octubre · 12:00–20:30h · Raul Clyde l · Miss Aletal · Exposición de fotografía · FRSH · RIMAS Room · Cine y gastronomía

articles.title: Week 5 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Packers need a win, but rival Bears are favored
articles.summary: The last time the Bears were favored at Lambeau Field was 2006.
articles.body:
Two years ago, the thought of the Chicago Bears being favored at Lambeau Field was hard to believe. Being favored with a backup quarterback was unfathomable.

But not only are the Bears favored with Tyson Bagent, it's hard to make a case for the Packers being the right pick.

Everything has changed in the NFL's oldest and most heated rivalry. Ben Johnson showed up in Chicago before last season with a confidence that belied the Bears' recent records. He called out the Packers and Matt LaFleur specifically. Then he has backed it up. The Bears are 14-7 since he arrived. They had a great comeback win against the Packers late in the regular season a year ago and a much more memorable comeback win over them in the playoffs. LaFleur is now getting constant heat from Packers fans and those losses to the Bears are a big part of it.

LaFleur is also taking plenty of blame for the Packers' malaise since Micah Parsons got hurt late last season. Counting that game in Denver when Parsons tore his ACL, the Packers are 2-7 since. This season they look like a mess. The offensive line has been terrible in pass protection and isn't opening lanes for the running game. Green Bay can't run the ball; the Packers have 232 rushing yards, which is 65 fewer than any other team. They're one of two teams with no rushing touchdowns. The defense is 24th in EPA allowed per play and success rate allowed as well. Nothing is good.

And yet, the Bears are favored by less than a field goal. Perhaps it's because Bagent was good but not great last week in his first start of the season. But the Bears ran the ball very well and dominated the Jets. The week before that they dominated the Eagles with Case Keenum at quarterback. The Bears haven't been a road favorite at Green Bay in 20 years . But it makes complete sense this week.

Nothing is a lock in the NFL, especially when dealing with desperate teams, playoff revenge and rivalries. But it's hard to make any logical argument why the Packers can beat the Bears on Sunday. Bears -2.5 is the pick. And if that happens, it'll get even noisier around LaFleur.

Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 5 of the NFL season:

It's not easy to lay this many points with the Cowboys, because their defense isn't trustworthy. But we know they'll score, and the same can't be said about the Buccaneers with undrafted rookie quarterabck Jalon Daniels for another week. Daniels did as well as he could last week in his first start, but this is not a situation conducive to the Bucs going on the road for a Thursday night game and playing well.

The lookahead line last week for this game in London was Jaguars -2.5 (via 4for4.com ), and the opening line had the Eagles favored by 1.5. A lot has changed of course. The Jaguars look great; grab a future on them to win the AFC or even Super Bowl before it's too late. The Eagles have been bad, especially on offense. Philadelphia has a ton of injuries, including running back Saquon Barkley and receiver DeVonta Smith, and offensive tackle Lane Johnson just retired. Still, it's a huge five-point shift from just last week, and probably an overreaction.

At some point, the Jameis Winston house of cards is coming down. The past two weeks, the Giants have needed interceptions deep in their own territory in the final seconds to barely squeeze out wins against the Titans and Cardinals at home. It's great that they're 3-1 but it's not going to continue. Jayden Daniels returns for the Commanders this week, and that will help a 1-3 Washington team that needs a win.

The Titans trailed 24-7 against the Ravens last week at halftime, when Lamar Jackson left the game with an ankle injury. So the Titans covering the spread last week shouldn't fool anyone (they crossed the finish line to cover 11.5 points with 1:12 to go). Now they face an 0-4 Texans team that has blown three games in the final two minutes and is desperate for a win. It could get ugly.

Maybe the Saints just aren't very good. They didn't look good in getting blown out by the Falcons on Monday night. But the Vikings have their own issues. They have scored one offensive touchdown in three weeks. They didn't score any against Miami last week, which is a sin against that Dolphins team. We're not giving up on this Saints team yet, especially at home.

Is Miami getting close to being in play for an upset? They trailed the 4-0 Chiefs by just seven points with three minutes left. They lost at the 4-0 Vikings by just five points. At the very least, they're fighting. The Bengals have looked lackluster the past couple weeks and might be without Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins this week. Let's say this: Don't assume picking against the Dolphins this week is a lock in your survival pools.

If you're a believer in the Browns, that's fine. But it's probably best to skip to the next game then. The Browns have won each of their last three games in the final four minutes, which is a lot of fun. But it's probably also not sustainable. And if you buy Deshaun Watson's resurgence, that's fine too. Let's say there should be some skepticism over that continuing. Last week's Jets performance at Chicago was absolutely brutal, but teams often play well after being embarrassed. The Jets are at home against a team that is 3-1 but probably not good. There's a reason they're favored.

In most scenarios, taking the Colts and the points would be the play. But don't ignore this: Pittsburgh played last Thursday and has extra rest, while the Colts played in London last week. Rest advantage/disadvantage is a factor in the NFL.

I still think the Raiders are a good team. But it's a tough spot this week, going to the East Coast for a 1 p.m. kickoff, off an emotional loss to the Chiefs and against a Patriots team that should feel like its season is back on track after a win over the Bills. The Raiders will be fine. But this isn't the best week for them.

Yes, it's scary to back the Chargers. They've been terrible. There are offensive line injuries. They tried to paint the second half against Seattle last week as the team showing fight and heart, but it was more like the Seahawks letting up after taking a 27-6 lead. But the Broncos haven't been good either. Their offense has been stuck. If the Chargers were going to break out of this stunning slump to start the season, this might be the time.

This is a fantastic game between two of the NFL's best teams (actually the top two in our NFL Power Rankings this week ). Taking the Seahawks is just respect for them, nothing against what the 49ers have done. Though, this is the 49ers' first true road game of the season, somehow.

The point spread is about right, giving the Seahawks the full field goal and nothing more. Seattle gets the slight nod, though it shouldn't surprise anyone if the 49ers win straight up, given how they've played. The 49ers did win at Seattle in Week 1 last season.

It's going to be hard to back the Lions this season. Their defense is simply bad right now. Any team getting points should score enough to stay in the game, and even if they don't they'll always be alive for a backdoor cover. Detroit can't stop anyone. The Cardinals can move the ball, and that's bad news for Detroit.

Last week, after Lamar Jackson left the game, the Ravens got outscored 11-0 at home against the Titans. They were sitting on a big lead but it was still a reminder that the Ravens are nowhere near the same team without the two-time MVP. The Falcons might not be the juggernaut they've looked like the past two games with Michael Penix Jr. back in the lineup, but they're a hot team that presumably doesn't need to face Jackson. It's a little surprising the line isn't higher.

Another very good game to end Week 5. The Rams haven't looked like the Super Bowl favorite yet this season. Last week's game at Philadelphia was ugly for 55 minutes, at least for the offense. But the Bills defense might be a problem too. It's 26th in DVOA and 29th EPA allowed per play . That could be a great thing for the Rams offense, which has been up and down. Josh Allen could just carry the Bills to a win, as he often does, but he'll need at least some help from a struggling defense.

articles.title: 2027 NFL mock draft 1.0: 5 quarterbacks land in Round 1, but WR Jeremiah Smith lands at No. 1
articles.summary: Here's an early look at how the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft might look, plus picks for the teams lacking first-round selections.
articles.body:
This is our first foray into projecting the 2027 NFL Draft class, and at first glance, it's shaping up to be an exciting first round (and beyond), with some marquee talents — more than each of the past two classes, it appears — at premium positions.

There are also four first-round picks already traded, and with the QB crowd, the pick movement should be a major storyline come April. Five quarterbacks landed in this first projection. There could be more in the next edition if Notre Dame's CJ Carr and Missouri's Austin Simmons keep progressing at the rates they are.

I didn't project any future trades here, and we're using the current draft order ( thanks, Tankathon ), which could change dramatically. It looks a little funny right now, but that's perfectly normal.

The goal here is to make as realistic of prospect pairings as possible now while also landing the players in the general range they might go. A lot will change between now and the draft, more than six months away, but this is how the early landscape is shaping up.

1. Houston Texans — Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

Smith is the best player in college football and might be the best prospect, regardless of position, in the past few draft cycles. I've been comparing him — mostly in terms of prospect rarity — to the likes of Andre Johnson and Julio Jones. Smith is a unicorn and should be a no-brainer top-five pick, even in a QB-heavy class. The Texans would be adding a Day 1 star.

2. Tennessee Titans — Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas

Robert Saleh's system is begging for a "Leo" rusher to make his defense more dangerous. Simmons, who had a 5.5-sack game against Tennessee, is a speed rusher with great get-off and bend. There's room for him to improve his technique, especially when taking on bigger blockers, and Simmons is not massive (6-foot-3, 246 pounds). But there is room on this defense for another Simmons, along with Jeffery.

3. Tampa Bay Buccaneers — Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame

The Bucs have limited their flexibility with the Baker Mayfield extension and would have a hard time moving him next season without a significant salary cap hit, but landing this high in the draft would lead to some interesting QB conversations come draft time. If they're less inclined to go that direction, drafting an elite corner such as Moore would be reasonable. He is one of the best CB prospects to come along since at least Sauce Gardner.

4. Los Angeles Chargers — Will Echoles, DT, Ole Miss

The Chargers are 0-4 and have several tough opponents remaining, so it'll be fascinating to see how far this talented team falls. LA's offense is a mess, but there are still defensive needs to consider. Almost all its pressures have come from the edge, and the Chargers really could use a difference maker such as Echoles inside.

Is he a top-five pick, though? I am not sure. Realistically, if the board fell like this, the Chargers would be entertaining trade-up calls for quarterbacks and trying to get a player such as Echoles farther down the line.

5. Miami Dolphins — Arch Manning, QB, Texas

There's a decent chance the Dolphins pass on a QB in 2027 and take an elite non-QB after investing in Malik Willis. If they finish in the top three picks, a trade down would be highly probable, especially if they could stay in range to draft someone such as the hometown hero Jeremiah Smith.

In this scenario they have to consider adding Manning and taking a similar approach to what the Raiders are doing this season with Fernando Mendoza. Manning has a pro-ready frame with quality traits and elite bloodlines, but the finished product isn't there.

For context, the Jets have all the ammunition they need to move up to No. 1 and take the QB of their choosing. They're better armed than any other team in terms of draft capital, and it will be fascinating to see how the eventual draft order shakes out and how many teams they might need to leapfrog.

Chambliss has already generated first-round buzz early in the college season despite some talent evaluators being more conservative on his projection over the summer. His age (24) and size (6-foot, 210 pounds) are limiting factors for some, but Chambliss' game features poise and some real magic. But barring something unforeseen, he's destined to go high. And I think Chambliss' floor is high, too.

7. New Orleans Saints — Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson

If Hampton runs well at the scouting combine, it would not be a stretch to see the 6-foot-2, 205-pound corner vault into this range of the draft. He's off to a terrific start to the season in spite of Clemson's struggles. Hampton really put the straps on Miami's Malachi Toney, who's arguably the best receiver in college football not named Jeremiah Smith. The Saints' corners have been picked on this season, so the need is high.

8. Washington Commanders — Yhonzae Pierre, Edge, Alabama

Pierre is another potential high riser in this class, especially if the uncertainty surrounding South Carolina's Dylan Stewart continues. The sacks haven't been rolling in so far for Pierre this season, but the pressures have, and he looked quite spry on his pick 6 against East Carolina. Rookie Sonny Styles has been a hit, but the Commanders could use another playmaker up front.

9. Arizona Cardinals — Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State

We'll have to see if Carson Beck can show enough this season to convince Arizona not to draft a quarterback. But if the Cardinals are picking in this range (or higher), it would be tough to pass up on an ascending talent such as Mestemaker. After a nightmare OSU debut at Tulsa, the North Texas transfer has wowed with his playmaking. He's well-built (6-foot-3, 215 pounds), fearless and can make all the throws, but Mestemaker is also green and can be fooled. Given his talent, however, I am starting to think the top 10 is his eventual destination.

10. Cincinnati Bengals — Ellis Robinson IV, CB, Georgia

Bengals cornerbacks DJ Turner II and Dax Hill are currently slated to hit free agency next spring, so adding more talent there figures to be on the to-do list. Robinson doesn't have tremendous size, but he reportedly has longer arms (33-inch range) for a 6-foot, 190-pound frame. UGA head coach Kirby Smart has said Robinson has added about 10 pounds from last season, and he has good feet, quality ball skills and scheme flexibility, perhaps even able to help in the slot some.

11. New York Jets (via Indianapolis Colts) — Jordan Seaton, OT, LSU

Maybe it's too early to move on from Olu Fashanu, but he had a nightmare game in Week 3 and seems to have regressed as a pass blocker. ESPN's Rex Ryan, a former Jets head coach, tore into Fashanu after the Lions loss, and that carries extra weight considering his son Seth is the Jets' passing-game coordinator. Awkward. Offensive tackles will be a premium again next draft, and Seaton appears to be the most natural pass blocker in the class. He's similar to the Vikings' Christian Darrisaw.

12. New York Jets (via Dallas Cowboys) — Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana

Three-for-three on offense? Maybe it won't go that way because the Jets' defense also remains undermanned in spots, but this would give Chambliss a stronger surrounding cast. Even with Garrett Wilson back, the Jets have limited reliable options at receiver, with injuries and inconsistency plaguing that position. Becker would add length and vertical prowess to the WR group, pairing up with his old IU running mate, Omar Cooper Jr.

13. Pittsburgh Steelers — Darian Mensah, QB, Miami

The Steelers can gamble on one of their young quarterbacks (Drew Allar, Will Howard) in a post-Aaron Rodgers world, addressing other needs and — if needed — waiting for what could be another strong QB class in 2028.

Or they could take college football's accuracy leader in Mensah, who might be a terrific fit in Mike McCarthy's system. Mensah throws with touch, timing and placement, and has excellent feel against pressure, even if his arm talent is a bit pedestrian.

14. Dallas Cowboys (via Green Bay Packers) — Cam Coleman, WR, Texas

Defense remains a huge worry, but they also could let George Pickens walk in free agency and fill his spot via the draft. Coleman hasn't been quite as productive so far as some thought he might be, but he would give Dallas another long, acrobatic target in Brian Schottenheimer's passing game.

15. Detroit Lions — Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina

Figuring out where Stewart fits in this class now — or whether he might stay in college — is trickier than it was a month ago. Stewart's suspension has raised some character questions, although it appears he's back on a track to return to playing . Stewart's production has also been somewhat underwhelming considering his rare gifts. If he can find a way to display those skills, this might be too tempting for Detroit to pass on. The Lions badly need a rusher to pair with Aidan Hutchinson.

16. Philadelphia Eagles — Trevor Goosby, OT, Texas

For years the Eagles have boasted great talent, depth and experience on the offensive line. That advantage hasn't been there this season. With Lane Johnson announcing his retirement , there's an opening at right tackle.

Goosby has been the Longhorns' left tackle the past two seasons and has right tackle experience from the 2024 season. He's a long-framed technician with good hand placement and enough footwork to cut off rush paths.

17. Atlanta Falcons — Trevor Lauck, OT, Iowa

With Jake Matthews turning 35 next offseason and Jawaan Taylor on a one-year deal, the Falcons have to bolster their OT depth. Lauck is a country-strong brawler who shines in the run game, although some scouts have questioned his lower-body power. Still, he'd be a force in a run-heavy attack in Atlanta and fill a need.

18. Denver Broncos — KJ Bolden, S, Georgia

I thought about an offensive tackle here, with Garett Bolles and Mike McGlinchey into their 30s, but the secondary also has some possible holes that might need filling next year. Bolden is a leaner-framed safety (6-foot, 195 pounds), but his range and athleticism stand out. He appears scheme- and role-versatile, tackles and closes on the ball very well and has two-plus years of quality tape in the SEC.

19. Carolina Panthers — Zabien Brown, CB, Alabama

Brown is a long, instinctive corner who has the skills to fit the Panthers' zone-heavy scheme. He's a willing tackler, although he's been sloppy against the run. He would be a good pairing opposite Jaycee Horn. Carolina's CB depth has been thinned considerably with Horn and Mike Jackson injured, so it's a good bet they'll be adding multiple corners next offseason.

20. New England Patriots — Trey'Dez Green, TE, LSU

The Patriots really could give Drake Maye another long, highly athletic target in the passing game. They've been especially poor in the red zone this season (outside of the Buffalo game) and could use someone such as the 6-foot-7 Green. You don't find many tight ends who can hit 21+ mph and catch the ball like he does; Green has even taken direct snaps in the backfield. He'd pair well with Eli Raridon, who's best suited in-line, with Hunter Henry in decline.

21. Cleveland Browns (via Los Angeles Rams) — Dante Moore, QB, Oregon

Moore is an accurate, anticipatory passer who thrives in structure and could be an excellent distributor in the Browns' system with a balanced array of weapons. He needs to find more consistent solutions against pressure. He returned to practice Monday after suffering a concussion Sept. 26 against USC, but he'll miss Saturday's game against UCLA .

This spring, there was talk he could have gone No. 2 overall to the Jets had Moore declared early. So why is he sitting at No. 21? There are more physically blessed prospects, and it's less about what Moore has done and more about how other QBs have generated more buzz recently in scouting circles. The Browns could afford to move up, if needed, for another quarterback, but I'd imagine this scenario would go over well there.

22. Cleveland Browns — Samson Okunlola, OT, Miami

Here's a fun projection, and perhaps it's a reach now, but Okunlola has impressed early. Despite being a top-20 national high school recruit, he's taken a longer road to a starting gig, rotating at left guard last season, yet he's earned the Canes' left tackle job this season and is thriving. I think everyone's patience could end up paying off in him being a high pick next April if he keeps progressing. The Browns could stand to upgrade over right tackle Tytus Howard, but Okunlola also could project inside if needed.

23. Las Vegas Raiders — Ryan Coleman-Williams, WR, Alabama

Coleman-Williams is a hotly debated prospect whose slew of drops last season tainted his reputation after an eye-opening freshman season in 2024 at age 17. The talent is still sky high, and Williams has displayed better hands (after another bad drop in Week 1 vs. East Carolina) this season. He's on pace for career-best numbers and profiles on the Jaylen Waddle/DeVonta Smith/Hollywood Brown spectrum. The Raiders must add as much explosive WR talent as possible to keep building up their offense.

24. Seattle Seahawks — Matayo Uiagalelei, Edge, Oregon

The Seahawks somehow have gone three straight draft cycles without drafting a true edge rusher, and it might effectively be a rebuild of that unit next season if Derick Hall is not re-signed. Uiagalelei is a physical, edge-setting force at 6-foot-5 and 272 pounds. He's cut from a similar cloth as DeMarcus Lawrence and Uchenna Nwosu.

25. Jacksonville Jaguars — Kingston Lopa, S, California

I thought about a linebacker here, but the Jaguars don't seem to be a strict-need team in the draft. General manager James Gladstone appears to favor talent and traits, and that leads us to Lopa, who is the FBS leader in interceptions (five), with a pick 6. At nearly 6-foot-5 and around 210 pounds, he's a lean but unique talent who could enter the draft early.

26. Buffalo Bills — Chris Cole, LB, Georgia

Linebacker has been mostly a Day 2 or 3 position for the Bills under general manager Brandon Beane, so it's no guarantee they'd take one in Round 1. Cole isn't exactly a thumper in the run game, but he's a fast closer and an excellent blitzer, and he'd potentially give the Bills a difference maker at this position, the kind they haven't had since Tremaine Edunds and Matt Milano.

27. New York Giants — David Stone, DT, Oklahoma

I thought about Oregon's A'Mauri Washington here, too, but I think Stone's versatility and upside make him a slightly more attractive fit right now. The Giants need to replenish some of their interior depth, and Stone could be a first-rounder if his knee checks out. He suffered a dislocated kneecap early in the season and has been able to play through it, but it appears to have slowed Stone down.

28. Chicago Bears — Kelley Jones, CB, Mississippi State

The Bears run man defense at a higher rate than most teams, and that's Jones' specialty. He's a long corner with ball skills who could help offset what they lost with Nahshon Wright moving on. Cornerback figures to be a position with some new faces in Chicago in 2027, with the futures of Jaylon Johnson and Kyler Gordon up in the air and Tyrique Stevenson's deal ending this season.

29. Baltimore Ravens — A'Mauri Washington, DT, Oregon

It's not a deep DT class right now, but Washington might still be the kind of player who slips to the end of Round 1 because of positional value. He also suffered an ankle injury against Oklahoma State and has been gritting through it the past few games, likely hurting his production. Washington has great mass at 6-foot-3 and 325 pounds, able to lift a unit's run defense and quick enough off the ball to add pass-rush value. He'd easily fit in as a potential replacement for 40-year-old Calais Campbell.

30. Minnesota Vikings — Jadan Baugh, RB, Florida

I don't know if the Vikings are prepared to use another first-round pick on a quarterback after quickly dumping J.J. McCarthy, but I could see them wanting to find answers at running back. Baugh is the lone back I currently see in the Round 1 picture, with his rare physicality, contact balance and three-down potential. He's not there yet with pass-pro proficiency, but Baugh has lofty potential as an explosive, yards-after-contact runner and receiver.

31. Kansas City Chiefs — Jamari Johnson, TE, Oregon

Johnson is a strong middle-of-the-field target with natural hands and a wide catch radius. His route-running wins on tempo and spatial awareness, which could work well with Patrick Mahomes — during on- and off-schedule plays. Travis Kelce has said it's his last season, and the Chiefs could use another higher-end talent at the position.

32. San Francisco 49ers — Greg Johnson, IOL, Minnesota

The Niners are a trickier team to project in the draft, but they have some OL questions that could lead them to a hulking guard in the mold of Johnson. He's a massive-framed blocker with surprising quickness in the run game and good anchor to hold up in pass protection inside.

42. Indianapolis Colts — KJ Duff, WR, Rutgers

A defensive tackle also would make sense, and several good ones could leak into the early parts of Round 2, but here the Colts select a small-forward type of pass-catcher who'd fit in nicely in between Alec Pierce, Josh Downs and Tyler Warren.

45. Green Bay Packers — Austin Siereveld, IOL, Ohio State

The Packers tend to draft tackles and move them inside, if needed, but Siereveld already has experience at both OG and OT spots. The Packers' OL issues have mounted this season, and they need as many promising solutions as possible.

52. Los Angeles Rams — Lance Heard, OT, Kentucky

The Rams could stand to add to the tackle talent pool. Heard has the length the Rams seem to favor, and even though his pass blocking remains a work in progress, he's already one of the best finishers in the run game in college football.

articles.title: The Eagles keep punting on the field. Are they now punting on the 2026 season?
articles.summary: The Eagles had high hopes entering the season, but things are already going sideways in Philadelphia.
articles.body:
Every once in awhile, you come across a statistic so damning, so indicative of a deeper problem that it glows. For the Philadelphia Eagles, that statistic is this: 0-for-12. That's the Eagles' third-down conversion rate last weekend in their collapse against the Rams.

Zero-for-12. Third-and-1, third-and-2, third-and-anything … the Eagles had 12 opportunities to keep drives alive in what would have been a defining win against Los Angeles, and fell short 12 times.

You know what usually happens when you can't get it done on third down, of course: You punt.

In the days after the Rams collapse, the Eagles saw two significant personnel developments that made observers wonder if the punting kept going after the game was done. On Tuesday, Lane Johnson, the 14-year veteran right tackle and franchise mainstay, announced his retirement , effective immediately. Johnson's departure means Philadelphia now has a major hole to fill on the line — not the situation you want to see when your team is already struggling offensively.

But Johnson's announcement was only the prelude to the week's big news: On Wednesday, the Eagles dealt guard/center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens for a pair of draft picks. When you're already facing significant struggles on that side of the ball, it's tough to rationalize trading a Pro Bowler for draft picks as anything other than a concession until those draft picks suit up.

If you're taking a long view, the Eagles' future looks bright. Philadelphia has four draft picks in the first two rounds of the 2028 draft thanks to the deals that sent Jurgens and A.J. Brown out of town. But those picks, who are currently toiling away in college, do exactly nothing for Philadelphia's needs right now … if in fact that's a primary concern for the Eagles.

Eagles GM Howie Roseman pushed back on the idea that the Jurgens trade is a sign that the 2-2 Eagles are folding the tents on 2026. "We're trying to win this year," he said Wednesday. "You want to have an extended run, and so my job is to look at how we can have sustained success for a long period of time, and you don't get many opportunities to get second-round picks in trades and get flexibility."

Yes, roster flexibility is definitely something fans prize when you're in the middle of a season and facing a depleted and winnable division.

Between the two departures this week and the fact that Pro Bowler Landon Dickerson remains on injured reserve, the Eagles are in real trouble along the offensive line. That's not a great sign for a team that's struggling to mount consistent drives. When you're not quite sure what you'll get out of your marquee running back, and you're still not sure if you have a good quarterback with bad tendencies or a bad quarterback with occasional highlights, well … that's not the foundation for a successful season.

The o-line square dance is a smokescreen for the Eagles' deep and persistent play-calling questions. The Eagles go through offensive coordinators like a hungry tourist devouring a Geno's cheesesteak, quickly and often messily. In the six years under head coach Nick Sirianni, the Eagles have had five OCs: Shane Steichen, Brian Johnson, Kellen Moore, Kevin Patullo and now Sean Mannion.

The pattern here isn't hard to determine: The OCs who guided Philadelphia to the Super Bowl, Steichen and Moore, have since moved on to head-coaching gigs of their own with Indianapolis and New Orleans, respectively. The OCs who haven't been able to get Philadelphia a win in the postseason have since just moved on, period.

All of which leads to the question of Sirianni's role and fate in all this. Yes, he's taken the Eagles to two Super Bowls and won one, which would seem to buy you a bit of grace. In many NFL cities, he'd have a guaranteed job for a decade. But this is Philly, where you're only as good as last week's result … and last week's result was worse than bad, it was embarrassing . That's a fast way to get the fans to turn on you, hard, and when that happens … it's time to start pricing movers, regardless of whether they have to bubble-wrap a Super Bowl trophy.

So far this season, Philadelphia has beaten Washington and Tennessee — two of the NFL's not-quite-juggernauts — by a total of six points, and gotten their doors blown off by Chicago and a Medicare-eligible Case Keenum. Given the chance to reset their season, the Eagles coughed up a 10-point lead over Los Angeles in the game's final four minutes.

Now, Philadelphia heads overseas to play the London — sorry, Jacksonville — Jaguars, followed by the Carolina Panthers and a run through all three other teams in the NFC East. That's the definition of a statement stretch — one way or another, we'll know who the Philadelphia Eagles are when they head into their Week 10 break. More importantly, we'll know whether they're worth paying attention to for the rest of 2026, or whether it'll be time to start hoping for better days in 2027 and beyond.

images.caption: Saquon Barkley is already banged up, while Nick Sirianni is yet again trying to figure out how to fix what's wrong with the Eagles. (AP Photo/Chris Szagola)

articles.title: Travis Kelce was supposed to be riding off into the sunset; instead, he's climbing the NFL record book
articles.summary: Travis Kelce caught only two passes in Las Vegas on Sunday, but that was enough to move past a Hall of Famer.
articles.body: Travis Kelce caught only two passes in Las Vegas on Sunday, but that was enough to move past a Hall of Famer. The Kansas City tight end entered the game tied with Tim Brown at 1,094 career receptions, then took sole possession of seventh place in the first half. The Chiefs beat the Raiders 30-27 to stay unbeaten at 4-0. Kelce finished with 15 yards on four targets, a quiet stat line on a night that carried real weight. He turned 37 the next day, in a season many thought would never happen.Travis Kelce is climbing the NFL record book fastSeventh place is only the start, and the names just ahead are close. Cris Carter is sixth with 1,101 catches. Marvin Harrison is fifth with 1,102. By my count, Kelce now sits at 1,096, five catches behind Carter and six behind Harrison. Four catches a game, which is roughly his pace this year, would put both behind him within two weeks.Jason Witten is another matter. He is fourth with 1,228. Catching him this year would take roughly 130 more receptions, and Kelce's best season ever is 110. That chase belongs to 2027, if there is one.There is a second record in play, and it says more about how he plays than any total does. Jason Kelce used his ESPN segment on Monday to point out that his younger brother passed Marshall Faulk, Terrell Owens and Steve Smith to take the career lead in yards after the catch. It is "hard to even fathom," Jason said. Yards after the catch comes down to balance and nerve, and Kelce has kept both at 37.Fewer catches, still a problem for defensesThe Vegas box score tells a different story from the record book. Four targets. Two catches. Fifteen yards. On its own, that line could feed worry about a fading star. In context, it looks like the price of a game Kansas City won on the ground.Kenneth Walker ran for 177 yards on 22 carries and scored twice, and his 76-yard run on the final play of the third quarter turned the game. Kansas City gained 189 yards on the ground as a team and Patrick Mahomes threw only 30 times, with both of his touchdown passes going to Thornton. The Raiders did contain Kelce. They could not contain everything else.That balance may be helping him. Through three games, before Vegas, Kelce had 14 catches on 18 targets for 231 yards and two touchdowns, a catch rate near 78 percent. Six targets a game is not a workhorse load, and he is catching most of them.What the next two weeks could settleRetirement talk has followed Kelce since January, and nothing has quieted it. Coverage of the Vegas trip called this his 14th and possibly final season. He has not said anything official.His life off the field has shifted too. He married Taylor Swift at Madison Square Garden in July, and Swift has missed Kansas City's road games so far because of an SNL appearance and the VMAs. Whether she makes the trip to Seattle on Oct. 25 is unknown.Kansas City hosts the Chargers on Oct. 18. Kelce needs five catches to pass Carter. articles.title: Sean Payton couldn't let Broncos offense continue to flounder with him not calling plays
articles.summary: The Broncos offense is in the bottom 10 in almost every category through four games.
articles.body:
When Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton handed off play-calling duties to Davis Webb this offseason, it made sense. Webb was a hot name in the offseason and the Broncos wanted to keep him.

Through four games of miserable offensive football, it no longer made sense to have a potential Hall of Fame coach not calling plays.

It appears Payton will be the primary play-caller again. There were matching reports from ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Media's Ian Rapoport on Thursday, both released at exactly noon Eastern time, and it's not hard to translate what is going on. Schefter said there will be a "collaborative play-calling approach" and Rapoport said the "process will remain collaborative," but Payton will be "more heavily involved in offensive play-calling this week" (Rapoport) and he will have an "increased role in the process" (Schefter) of calling plays. Webb, Denver's offensive coordinator, will be "continuing with a significant game-planning and game-day role" (Schefter) with "a major voice on game day and during the week" (Rapoport) going forward.

In other words, Payton is taking back play-calling duties, though it's unclear if he'll be doing it all or just most of it.

It's easy to see why the Broncos want to massage that message through the media. Webb came back to the Broncos after getting interviews elsewhere, got four games to call plays and Payton took back control of the offense.

It's an abrupt move but after four games, Payton had little choice.

Payton was clearly not comfortable giving up play-calling duties. He had been the primary play-caller on offense every season he has been on the sideline as head coach. The Broncos hadn't even finished the first game, an ugly loss to the Chiefs, before there was speculation he'd be calling plays before long.

The Broncos offense started the season poorly and aside from good second halves against the Jaguars and Rams, it has not improved. Denver had just 13 first-half points in four games. That was the second-worst through four games over the last five NFL seasons, according to Josh Dubow of the Associated Press . The 2023 Giants had just nine first-half points through four weeks.

Denver is 26th in offensive success rate . Denver is averaging 3.6 yards per rushing attempt, tied for fifth-worst in the NFL. The Broncos average 6.1 yards per pass attempt, tied for fourth-worst in the NFL. Bo Nix's numbers are down across the board, including a passer rating that is 80.4 after he was 87.8 last season. The Broncos traded a first-round pick and more to get receiver Jaylen Waddle, and in three of Denver's four games he combined for 47 yards.

Payton is masterful calling plays. He is one of the best of his era. The Broncos were 2-2, and probably fortunate to be .500, and he couldn't sit back while the offense floundered.

The NFL is a results league, and the results weren't good enough for Webb to keep controlling the offense.

Sean Payton has strong history calling plays

Webb is 31 years old and considered one of the hottest young assistants in the NFL. This past offseason he got head-coaching interviews. The real danger for the Broncos was losing him to another team that would make him a play-calling offensive coordinator. The switch was made. Webb stayed in Denver.

His month of calling Denver's plays, and the ineffectiveness, could cool down his market next offseason. It's also not the end of the world for Webb. In 2002, New York Giants head coach Jim Fassel took back play-calling duties from his young, hotshot offensive coordinator. That was Payton who got demoted, and his career turned out fine.

"I like Sean Payton and I feel like in some ways we let him down," then Giants tight end and current Lions coach Dan Campbell told the New York Post in 2002. "You can't deny we're not putting up points but I can't sit here and go, 'It's Sean Payton's fault' because I dang well know it's not."

It's not all Webb's fault for the 2026 Broncos, but Payton making a move was inevitable.

The Broncos were 14-3 last season and while they were due to regress, the first four games have sent warning signals that things were going to get worse before they got better. The Chiefs are already 4-0 in the AFC West and the 3-1 Raiders are much improved. The Broncos couldn't lose much more ground, and it would have been an unforced error to do so while Payton wasn't calling plays.

Payton's offenses have finished in the top 10 in yards gained 16 times in his first 21 seasons as a head coach or offensive coordinator, and 13 times it finished in the top 10 in points scored. The Broncos are 27th in both categories this season.

Maybe Payton calling more plays won't completely turn things around. But he wasn't going to wait any longer to find out.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels latest injury update: Washington QB expected to suit up for Week 5 clash vs New York Giants after missing two games with elbow injury
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels wants to quiet the noise surrounding his elbow injury. It took up a lot of space in 2025; he clearly doesn’t want that for 2026.
articles.body: Jayden Daniels wants to quiet the noise surrounding his elbow injury. It took up a lot of space in 2025; he clearly doesn’t want that for 2026. So, what does he do? He consults experts and sees specialists. He wants to get back on the gridiron as quickly as he can make it happen.The wait is finally over. He got injured in Week 2, but after taking care of his elbow, probably much better than how he did in 2025, he’s set for a Week 5 comeback! Talk about missing just a few games when the whole world predicted weeks’ worth of absence!Jayden Daniels expected to return in Week 5 vs New York GiantsESPN reporter John Keim asked Washington Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough if Jayden Daniels is ready for Week 5 vs. the New York Giants. The OC said, “He’s full go.” The 25-year-old LSU alum practiced full Wednesday with a brace on his non-throwing left elbow.As per NFL Insider Adam Schefter, the game-breaking quarterback is “probably” going to require surgery over the 2027 offseason. He is delaying the procedure so he gets to remain available for the 2026 season.Jayden Daniels could be prone to injuring elbow againThe poised signal-caller Jayden Daniels told reporters on Wednesday that he considers the elbow brace a part of him now. The more he does that, the more comfortable he gets with his injury-prone elbow.Because, as fate would have it, he fell the same way to the ground on his elbow as he did in 2025. And he suffered the same injury twice. To top it off, he is returning now, just like he did return from an elbow injury in 2025.The only real possibility for the introverted QB is that he could re-injure his dislocated elbow. If he does, history will repeat itself for the second time! He also played in 2025 after injuring his elbow. And he re-injured it after returning from recovery. If the same happens again in 2026…we don’t know what to type here!Jayden Daniels injury risk and Commanders QB optionsAccording to DraftSharks, the Washington Commanders' explosive quarterback has a “low” injury risk in 2026. He has a 41% chance of injury in the 2026 season, which is a 3.1% chance of injury per game. He was projected to miss 1.2 games in 2026, but he’s already missed two in four games.His durability score is 2.83. 5 is the highest. The durability score is what stands out. If it had been around 3 or 4, or even 4.5, the Commanders could have been carefree. But it’s near 2. And that’s what makes Jayden Daniels’ return scarier than ever.If he returns with a dislocated elbow that “probably” requires surgery, there are chances that he could re-injure it. Then, what will Washington do? They may have to look for options.Mac Jones and Mason Rudolph could be explored for WashingtonOptions like available quarterbacks. Like Mac Jones, who sits behind healthy Brock Purdy in the San Francisco 49ers. Or Mason Rudolph, who sits behind ever-healthy Aaron Rodgers in the Pittsburgh Steelers. Or any other QB who is available.Jayden Daniels’ backup, Marcus Mariota, is also injured! He suffered an MCL sprain in his right knee in the Week 4 loss to the Indianapolis Colts. He was not placed on injured reserve. But he is expected to miss a few games.The Commanders are in dire need of a QB! Who’s it going to be? That will save their 2026 season…? Only time will tell. Or will they rely on Athan Kaliakmanis, the 2026 rookie who may shine as Jayden Daniels did in his 2024 rookie season? We never know what the future holds for Washington.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “WTF happened to Kay Adams?”: Fans react to bizarre facial expressions during Rob Gronkowski interview
articles.summary: Kay Adams has found herself at the center of an unexpected NFL social media moment after a clip from Up & Adams began circulating online, her facial
articles.body: Kay Adams has found herself at the center of an unexpected NFL social media moment after a clip from Up & Adams began circulating online, her facial expressions during a conversation with Rob Gronkowski caught everyone’s eye. The segment was supposed to be about Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers. Instead, Adams’ reactions quickly became the thing fans were talking about.Kay Adams leaves NFL fans baffled with bizarre facial expressions during Gronk interviewGronkowski appeared on Up & Adams to discuss the Chargers’ struggles and offered a blunt assessment of Herbert’s situation. The former NFL tight end argued that Los Angeles is not putting its star quarterback in the right offensive system. According to Gronkowski, the Chargers’ scheme is too complicated and does not fully take advantage of Herbert’s biggest strengths.His comments came as the Chargers continued to struggle, with Herbert completing 59.7% of his passes for four touchdowns and six interceptions through the team’s first four games. Gronkowski's argument was essentially that the quarterback should not be taking all the blame for the team's problems.But while Gronkowski was breaking down Herbert’s situation, something else was happening on screen.Throughout the conversation, Adams appeared extremely animated, pulling a variety of exaggerated expressions as Gronkowski made his points.At different moments, she started smirking and smiling.That made fans go: “WTF happened to Kay Adams?”Rather than becoming another routine NFL debate about Herbert, the segment turned into a social media discussion about Adams’ reactions.The irony is that Gronkowski was making a fairly serious football argument. Yet the internet had other priorities. For many fans, it was less about whether Gronkowski was right about Herbert and more about trying to figure out what Adams was thinking while listening to him. His main point was that the Chargers need to build an offense around Herbert’s skill set instead of forcing the quarterback to operate in a system that does not suit him. With Los Angeles sitting at 0-4, the criticism comes at a particularly difficult point in the season.Adams is no stranger to being a recognizable face in NFL media, but this particular moment caught fans off guard because of just how expressive she appeared during the discussion.There is no indication from the clip that anything was actually wrong with Adams. Her expressions could simply have been natural reactions to Gronkowski’s comments. Still, social media rarely needs much more than funny expressions. For now, Gronkowski’s controversial take on the Chargers and Herbert remains the substance of the segment but Kay Adams’ facial expressions are what appear to have won the internet’s attention.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ father can’t simply walk into Arrowhead to watch his son. Here’s why
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes’ father, Pat Mahomes Sr., will be able to watch his son take the field at Arrowhead Stadium, but there is a catch.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes’ father, Pat Mahomes Sr., will be able to watch his son take the field at Arrowhead Stadium, but there is a catch. The former MLB pitcher has reportedly been granted permission to travel to Kansas City to attend Patrick Mahomes’ Chiefs home games while he remains on probation. However, his trips come with a strict condition that makes his plans to watch his son play anything but routine.Patrick Mahomes’ dad faces unusual condition to watch son at ArrowheadMahomes Sr. has agreed to undergo urine testing before and after his trips when requested by his probation officer. The unusual arrangement stems from his ongoing probation following his DWI case. While the court has allowed him to make the trip to Kansas City for Chiefs home games, his request to travel to certain road games was not granted.For Mahomes Sr., the ruling means he can still be in the stands at Arrowhead to support his son during the Chiefs’ home games. That permission is significant because his probation has placed restrictions on his ability to travel. Rather than having unrestricted access to Chiefs games, his travel plans remain subject to the conditions imposed by the court.The testing requirement adds another layer to what would ordinarily be a simple trip to watch his son play football. Mahomes Sr. has reportedly completed 160 hours of community service and an outpatient alcohol-treatment program as part of his probation. His probation officer has also reported no issues with his alcohol-monitoring device or drug and alcohol testing.Pat Mahomes Sr. can watch Patrick at Arrowhead, but road games are differentThe court's decision does not give Mahomes Sr. unrestricted freedom to follow the Chiefs around the country. He reportedly sought permission to travel to Kansas City, Las Vegas and Cincinnati to attend games. While Kansas City was approved, the requests involving the road trips were not.That leaves Arrowhead as the place where Mahomes Sr. can continue one of his most familiar roles: watching his son compete in front of the Chiefs’ home crowd. For Patrick Mahomes, having his father in the stands is nothing new. But this time, getting to Arrowhead requires his dad to follow a very different set of rules.And that unusual condition could make every Chiefs home game a little more significant for the Mahomes family.Why Pat Mahomes Sr. is still on probationMahomes Sr.’s current restrictions date back to his DWI case. He was arrested in Texas in February 2024 on a DWI charge and later pleaded guilty to a third-or-more DWI offense. He was sentenced to five years of probation.His legal troubles continued in 2026 when he was arrested over an alleged probation violation, leading to additional scrutiny of his compliance with the terms of his probation. Despite that history, his recent progress appears to have allowed him some additional flexibility, including permission to travel to Kansas City for his son’s home games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jets missing 2 key players at practice ahead of NFL Week 5 matchup vs Browns
articles.summary: The Jets could be in for a tough game this weekend against the Browns after latest injury update.
articles.body:
The New York Jets continue to deal with significant injury concerns heading into their NFL Week 5 matchup against the Cleveland Browns, with two important offensive players still absent from practice Thursday.

Breece Hall (quad), Adonai Mitchell (finger) not seen participating in practice again Thursday, per @Al_Iannazzone. — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 8, 2026

Breece Hall (quad), Adonai Mitchell (finger) not seen participating in practice again Thursday, per @Al_Iannazzone.

Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 8, 2026

Running back Breece Hall and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell were both not seen participating during the early portion of Thursday's practice.

Breece Hall remains sidelined with quad injury

Aug 14, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Jets running back Breece Hall (20) carries the ball against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images

Hall continues to work his way back from a quadriceps injury that forced him to miss New York's Week 4 loss to the Chicago Bears. The running back was not present for warmups Thursday, marking another missed practice as he attempts to return for Sunday's matchup with Cleveland.

Jets head coach Aaron Glenn previously described Hall's injury as week-to-week, and his continued absence makes it increasingly difficult to envision him being ready to play Sunday without a significant change over the next 48 hours. Hall initially suffered the injury during New York's Week 3 loss to the Detroit Lions.

If Hall cannot return, Braelon Allen would once again be expected to handle the bulk of the Jets' running back workload. Allen handled all 16 touches given to New York running backs in the Week 4 loss to Chicago, finishing with 14 carries for 59 yards along with two receptions for eight yards.

Adonai Mitchell also misses another practice

Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Mitchell is facing a similar situation at wide receiver. The young receiver was not present for Thursday's warmups because of a finger injury, putting him on track to miss another practice ahead of Sunday's game.

Mitchell has already missed the Jets' last two games after suffering the finger injury in practice. Glenn said Wednesday that Mitchell remains week-to-week, while the specific nature of the injury has not been disclosed.

The continued absence of both Hall and Mitchell is especially concerning for a Jets offense that struggled badly in Chicago. New York managed just 157 total yards and 12 points in the 23-12 loss, while quarterback Geno Smith completed only 8 of 15 passes for 119 yards.

The Jets will have another opportunity to get both players on the field Friday before final injury designations are announced. New York enters Sunday's matchup at 1-3, while the Browns are 3-1 and have won three straight.
